notes: Implement (product spec, no bug.patch): per-project milestones — unique names (case-insensitive, closed ones included), an open-milestone cap, issues placed into an open milestone of their own project at creation or later, progress over every live issue, overdue on a strict boundary, closing that moves only open live work to another open milestone (or out) and tells each moved assignee once, reopening, three domain events audited, a new notification kind. Reference solution: 32 source files + 4 visible test fixtures, 821 changed lines across config, types (common, issue, milestone, event, notification, activity), zod (common, issue, milestone, notification, activity), drizzle schema (new milestones table, issues.milestone_id, activity subject enum, notification kind enum) + the embedded migration, mappers, a new milestone repository, issue-repository (setIssueMilestone, countMilestoneProgress as two COUNT queries, moveOpenIssuesBetweenMilestones as one UPDATE … RETURNING over open live rows), lib/milestones (MilestoneStateError, open/overdue/name helpers), lib/errors, milestone-service, issue-service (gate shared by createIssue and setIssueMilestone, issue.updated on a move), notification-service (milestone.closed fan-out per moved issue through notify, so preferences and the actor exclusion apply), activity-service (three listeners), the two UI label records the Record types force, and the barrels. Why hard: the rules interact across eight layers; the gate that an issue's milestone must be an open milestone of its own project has two entry points (creation and a later move) and the natural place to put it is the move; progress and the move on close must be counts and a set-based UPDATE, since the issue list caps every page at 100; closing must move open live issues only (done, canceled and archived ones stay) and the alert must go through notify() so the closer is excluded and each assignee hears once per issue; the open/closed state has replay rules (close twice, reopen an open one) and the cap counts open milestones only; overdue is a strict comparison. Traps: scale (naive B, progress read off a page of 100 of the project's issues: fails the 150-issue progress case and the 120-issue close); wrong place (naive C, the gate only in setIssueMilestone: fails "applies the same gate when the milestone is given at creation"); second cause (naive D, the close moves every live issue of the milestone, finished ones included: fails the move case, the alert case and the empty-milestone case); replay (naive E, no state check on close/reopen: fails "refuses to close twice or reopen an open milestone"); boundary (naive F, overdue at the target instant: fails the overdue case). Hidden test: 21 cases, fake Date pinned to 2026-07-01T09:00Z, real id generator, logger and rate limiter, throwaway database built through the repositories. Validation: pristine tsc 0 / 617 pass; pristine + hidden: the file cannot load (new modules missing) → fail; pristine + solution.patch (patch -p1 clean): tsc 0, hidden 21/21 x3, full 638/638 x2; naive B 2/21 fail; naive C 1/21; naive D 3/21; naive E 1/21; naive F 1/21.
